course_description:
Techniques involved in systematic food product development.

Successful food product development requires a knowledge of a range of disciplines as well as a systematic approach to the development process. Integration of marketing and consumer aspects with the technical aspects of food processing and food products is very important. ﾠThis course provides the students with an understanding of the need for product development and the triggers for new food products. It covers the various stages involved in product development as well as the food regulations and approval procedure for new products. Students gain the knowledge of techniques that can be applied in systematic product development to maximise the chances of success of new food products in the marketplace.

Importantly, this course covers application of the theoretical aspects into practising product development during the tutorials. Students will be guided through the various stages of product development and will work in groups to develop a new food product at lab scale. The practical labs will provide an opportunity to gain hands-on experience in applying some of the theoretical knowledge in practice.

The course comprises of weekly 2-hour lectures and 2-hour tutorial. From week 7 onwards, 3 hours practical labs will replace the tutorial. For the practical labs, some of the basic ingredients would be provided. However, depending on the project the student decides to do, the student may have to provide the additional ingredients.ﾠ

At the School of Agriculture and Food Sustainability, we are committed to creating an inclusive and empowering learning environment for all students. We value and respect the diverse range of experiences our students bring to their education, and we believe that this diversity is crucial for fostering a rich culture of knowledge-sharing and meaningful exploration. We hold students and staff accountable for actively contributing to establishing a respectful and supportive learning environment.

Bullying, harassment, and discrimination in any form are strictly against our principles and against ﾠ UQ Policy, ﾠand will not be tolerated. If you have any concerns about your experience in this course, we encourage you to tell a member of the course teaching team. Your well-being and a positive learning atmosphere are of utmost importance to us.

learning_outcomes.description: Apply core concepts of the new product development process to solve problems and address real-world scenarios in food product development.
Use knowledge of the new product development process to design a product development Brief.
Review food product ingredients to determine nutrition information.

assessment_details.task_description: Task Description: This is a group assignment. Each group comprising five (5) students (self-selected using the course Blackboard Ultra site) are required to develop a detailed product design brief for a proposed new food product, by applying concepts and knowledge developed throughout lectures and tutorials. The report should include analysis and interpretation of market research results, idea generation and justification of the selected concept, concept statement, idea screening and evaluation process, and a comprehensive product brief that will serve as the blueprint for the proposed new product. Students are expected to apply food science, consumer, and market knowledge in developing the product concept, with decisions and justifications supported by relevant literature, market trends, and/or industry evidence where appropriate. This assessment represents the planning and concept development stage of the semester-long New Product Development project and will provide the foundation for subsequent prototype development and evaluation activities later in the course. Assessment will consider both the quality of the final report and the successful completion of project milestones throughout the semester, including the idea generation stage and the product's concept statement. The report should be 1200–1500 words in length (excluding references and appendices). This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use Artificial Intelligence (AI) and/or Machine Translation (MT) tools, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which AI or MT will provide only limited support and guidance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. To pass this assessment, students will be required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of their written submission independent of AI and MT tools. Report Contents: The report will contain the following section: Title page - including group members' names and ID and product name. Declaration of AI or MT use (if any). Introduction Idea generation Screening process and selected idea Concept statement Detailed product brief of the selected idea: should provide elaborate explanation for each feature of the selected idea. Reference list. It is suggested to use APA 7th referencing style. Appendix (if any). Further details on the report structure and guidelines are provided via Blackboard Ultra. Assessment Breakdown: Milestone achievements: 3% (each milestone weigthed 1.5%) New Food Product Design Brief Report: 12% Marking rubric and criteria are provided via Blackboard Ultra Tutorial Attendance: As tutorial activities support the development of the product concept and brief, regular attendance and active participation in tutorials are strongly recommended to support successful completion of the assessment tasks. assessment_details.title: Food Labelling Report
assessment_details.category: Paper/ Report/ Annotation, Tutorial/ Problem Set
assessment_details.task_description: Task Description: This is an individual assignment. Students will be provided with a randomly assigned food product formulation and will be required to develop components of a food label in accordance with relevant food regulatory requirements and standards. Following the label development, students are required to critically evaluate the product formulation and completed label to identify and justify any claims that may be made under FSANZ regulations, including nutritional claims, health claims, and other permitted claims where applicable. Students must demonstrate understanding of ingredient composition, nutrient calculations, and regulatory requirements when determining the suitability of these claims. The assignment will involve interpretation and application of food labelling regulations, including preparation of mandatory labelling information and evaluation of the suitability of claims that may be associated with the product. The assessment is designed to develop students’ understanding of food labelling compliance, nutrient composition, and regulatory considerations in food product development. Marking rubric and criteria are provided via Blackboard Ultra. This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use Artificial Intelligence (AI) and/or Machine Translation (MT) tools, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which AI or MT will provide only limited support and guidance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. To pass this assessment, students will be required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of their written submission independent of AI and MT tools. The use of AI or MT must be referenced appropriately. Please see assessment guidelines in blackboard course site for specific instructions. Report Contents and Details: Title page - including student name and ID and formulation number. Declaration of AI or MT use (if any). Parts of mandatory food label - including nutrition information panel (NIP), ingredient list, allergen summary statement and claims. Explanation and justifications on the claims included in the label. Explanations and calculations used to create the NIP. Reference list. It is suggested to use APA 7th referencing style. Appendix - including, but not limited to, label of the custom ingredients, reference product, and others. Further details of the report are provided via Blackboard Ultra. assessment_details.task_description: Task Description: This assessment requires students to work in groups (the same group from New Food Product Design Brief Report ). During practical classes, students will work through the stages of the New Product Development (NPD) process to develop a product prototype within an assigned category, guided by the product brief developed earlier. Groups will refine their formulation, processing methods, and product characteristics through practical development and evaluation activities. The final report should document and justify the development process undertaken by the group, including formulation decisions, processing development, sensory evaluation, packaging considerations, and scale-up considerations. Students are expected to apply food science, consumer, and market knowledge throughout the project, with decisions and justifications supported by relevant literature and experimental observations. Each member of the group will be responsible and graded for writing one part of the report as well as contributing to the overall report. Assessment will consider both the quality of the final report and the successful completion of prototype development milestones. Additionally, a peer assessment will be used to evaluate contributions. This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use Artificial Intelligence (AI) and/or Machine Translation (MT) tools, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which AI or MT will provide only limited support and guidance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. To pass this assessment, students will be required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of their written submission independent of AI and MT tools. The use of AI or MT must be referenced appropriately. Please see assessment guidelines in blackboard course site for specific instructions. Report Structure: The report will contain the following section: Title page Legal declaration Introduction - written by the group (word count limit: 300 ± 10% words) Ingredient selection and formulation - written by Student 1 Process development and cost calculation - written by Student 2 Sensory attributes and evaluation - written by Student 3 Packaging, labelling and shelf life - written by Student 4 Scale up - written by Student 5 Reflection - written by the group (word count limit: 250 ± 10% words) All parts of the report must be compiled and submitted as one report. Word limit: each individually written part should have 1000 ± 10% words, excluding references and appendix. Each of the individually written part must have its own reference list, using APA 7th referencing style. Further details on the report structure, templates and guidelines are provided via Blackboard Ultra. Assessment Breakdown: Final report: 25%, consist of: Individual part of the report: 20% Group part of the report: 3% Peer assessment: 2% Marking rubric and criteria are provided via Blackboard Ultra Practical Attendance As product prototype development and evaluation are conducted during practical classes, attendance and active participation in practical sessions are essential for successful completion of the final report.
